system_description.narrative_title: Energy-driven market volatility and sector rotation
system_description.narrative_summary: A surge in energy prices and evolving energy-demand dynamics (including AI-related power needs) are driving renewed market volatility and forcing rapid sector rotation across global equities. The shock to energy markets is propagating through inflation expectations, central-bank focus, commodity prices and investor behaviour—pressuring tech and growth stocks, boosting energy/defense and commodity plays, and pushing capital into perceived havens.
system_description.scope: Global financial markets over the Oct 25–27 news window: equity sector performance and flows (tech, energy, defense, cyclicals), commodity markets (oil, gas, gold, base/rare metals), investor cohorts (retail, hedge funds, institutional), corporate earnings/signals, and short-term policy/market catalysts that connect energy shocks to asset prices.
system_description.super_system: Global economy and geopolitics, especially energy security dynamics and macroeconomic/monetary policy responses
adjacent_subsystems: Energy commodity markets and supply chains (oil, gas, rare earths, renewables recycling)
Equity market structure and investor behaviour (retail flows, hedge funds, sector rotation)
Central banking, inflation expectations and bond markets

variables.name: Energy price level
variables.description: The aggregated market price level of energy commodities (broadly capturing oil, gas and other fuels) measured on a continuous index scale.

variables.name: Energy price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability of energy commodity prices, measured as continuous price dispersion or realized/implied volatility.

variables.name: AI-driven power demand
variables.description: The evolving rate of electricity consumption attributable to large-scale computing and AI workloads, measured as a continuous growth/process variable.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The market and public expectation of future inflation measured on a continuous forecast horizon (e.g., 1–5 year expected inflation).

variables.name: Monetary policy stance
variables.description: The prevailing tightness or looseness of monetary policy as reflected by expected policy leanings and communication, represented on a continuous scale.

variables.name: Real interest rate level
variables.description: The inflation-adjusted interest rate environment (real yields) across relevant maturities, measured continuously.

variables.name: Equity market volatility
variables.description: The market-wide variability of equity prices (aggregate volatility index or realized volatility) measured continuously.

variables.name: Sector rotation rate
variables.description: The pace at which capital reallocates between equity sectors (relative weight changes across sectors) measured as a continuous flow/process metric.

variables.name: Flows to safe assets
variables.description: The net rate of capital moving into perceived safe-haven asset classes (e.g., sovereign debt, gold, cash equivalents) measured continuously as net flows.

variables.name: Sector valuation gap
variables.description: The cross-sectional difference in valuation multiples between advantaged and disadvantaged sectors, measured as a continuous spread.

variables.name: Investor risk appetite
variables.description: The aggregate willingness of investors to accept risk for return, measured as a continuous sentiment/behavioral index.

variables.name: Retail equity flow
variables.description: The net rate of retail investor capital entering or exiting equity markets, measured continuously as flow volume or proportion.

variables.name: Hedge fund leverage
variables.description: The aggregated leverage exposure of hedge funds and similar active strategies measured as a continuous ratio or level of borrowed/derivative exposure.

variables.name: Commodity supply disruption risk
variables.description: The assessed probability and magnitude of supply-side disruptions across key commodities (energy, metals) measured as a continuous risk index.

variables.name: Earnings revision trend
variables.description: The directional rate at which corporate earnings expectations are being revised up or down across the market, measured as a continuous trend/process.

variables.name: Currency strength index
variables.description: The broad value of the reference currency against a basket of peers, measured continuously and capturing currency-driven purchasing power changes.

catalysts.title: Near-term Fed policy decision
catalysts.description: An imminent Federal Reserve policy decision and communication is likely to move markets around the upcoming meeting, driving volatility and updates to rate expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines cite markets 'ahead of Fed meeting' and 'Fed decision in focus' (Gold rises as lower oil prices ease inflation fears ahead of Fed meeting; Gold gains on softer oil prices; Fed decision in focus).

catalysts.title: Short-term oil price swing and corrections
catalysts.description: Recent moves to multi-month highs followed by technical pullbacks indicate ongoing oil price swings that will drive energy volatility and market reallocation in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines note oil hitting multi-month highs and then technical corrections (oil hits highest in nearly six months; Oil Declines on Likely Technical Correction; U.S. Stocks Fall as Oil Prices Hit Five-Month High).

catalysts.title: Imminent AI-driven power demand increase
catalysts.description: Growing AI workloads create an accelerating electricity demand trend ('AI power crunch') that can boost energy-sector cash flows and prompt sector reallocation.
catalysts.rationale: Headline warns of an 'imminent AI power crunch' and energy stocks positioned to profit (These energy stocks are poised to profit from an imminent AI power crunch).

catalysts.title: Retail investor pullback from equities
catalysts.description: Retail investors are showing increased caution and reduced inflows, which can amplify volatility and reduce breadth during market stress.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Retail investors are getting cold feet about stocks, just when the market needs them most.'

catalysts.title: U.S. midterm election (vote and post-vote reaction)
catalysts.description: U.S. midterm results and the immediate market reaction are likely to alter risk appetite and safe-haven flows regardless of outcome.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Relief may be coming after the midterms — no matter who wins,' implying reduced uncertainty post-election.

catalysts.title: IEA projects sustained elevated energy markets
catalysts.description: IEA guidance that energy markets won't return to pre-war levels in 2027 supports market pricing of a prolonged higher-energy baseline, affecting inflation and commodity risk.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'IEA's Birol does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027.'

catalysts.title: Trend hedge funds' de-risking after AI selloff
catalysts.description: Recent losses at trend funds from AI stock weakness increase the risk of systematic de-risking and leverage reduction, feeding volatility and faster sector moves.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trend hedge funds saw worst week since 2024 as AI stocks fell,' indicating de-risking potential.
